correctness.rationale: Coordinate-antiderivative tests give the three conditional expectations. Their expectations force E[x^2]=2c^2, hence the exact mean–variance shell. Endpoint and one-sided-threshold equality reduce invariant support to the two equilibria. The nonlinear forcing residual equals -2 zdot, giving the exact variance defect and zero covariance. Zero defect forces constant z, then bounded completeness forces y=z=0 and x^2=2c^2. The packaged checker verifies all algebraic identities.

value.rationale: The Michelson system is a canonical reversible reduction of the steady Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation whose literature emphasizes periodic, quasi-periodic, homoclinic, and chaotic bounded dynamics. The theorem gives all of those compact recurrent states a common exact RMS amplitude, converts that into a sharp barycenter–variance shell, and forces every non-equilibrium stationary state to occupy both sides of the equilibrium amplitude. For periodic orbits this becomes a concrete crossing law, while the vertical forcing defect supplies an exact dynamical consistency check. These are structural statements rather than a numerical orbit statistic.
